name: Suya
description: Skewered beef or chicken rubbed with a spiced groundnut paste, grilled over open charcoal. Lagos's definitive night-market classic.

name: Boli
description: Unripe plantain roasted directly on charcoal until the skin blackens and the inside becomes sweet and smoky. Served with groundnut or pepper sauce.

name: Akara
description: Deep-fried balls of blended black-eyed peas seasoned with onion, pepper, and crayfish. A beloved Lagos breakfast staple.

name: Puff Puff
description: Fluffy, deep-fried dough balls lightly sweetened and served hot. Found at virtually every street corner in Lagos.

name: Pepper Soup
description: A piping hot, intensely spiced broth with catfish, goat meat, or offal. The complex pepper-blend base is legendary for its warming, curative properties.

name: Ogi (Akamu)
description: Smooth fermented corn or millet porridge served warm, often alongside Akara or Moi Moi. A gentle, nourishing morning staple.

name: Fried Yam
description: Thick-cut yam slices deep-fried to golden perfection and served with fried fish or pepper sauce. A filling, comforting classic.

name: Moi Moi
description: Steamed bean pudding made from blended black-eyed peas with egg, fish, or corned beef folded in. Nutritious and deeply savory.

name: Roasted Corn
description: Whole corn cobs roasted over charcoal until slightly charred, often paired with ube (African pear) during the season.

name: Nkwobi
description: Cow foot slow-cooked until tender, then tossed in a rich spiced palm oil paste with utazi leaves. A celebrated bar and nighttime delicacy.

name: Agege Bread
description: Soft, pillowy white bread with a slightly sweet crumb and chewy crust. Lagos's most iconic bread, named after the district where it originated.

name: Banga Soup
description: A rich, aromatic palm nut soup cooked with assorted meats and spiced with dried herbs. Heavenly with starch or eba.

name: Kilishi
description: Thin-sliced beef coated in a spiced groundnut paste, sun-dried, then briefly grilled. The Northern Nigerian answer to jerky — chewy, fiery, addictive.

name: Coconut Candy
description: Grated coconut caramelized with sugar and shaped into bite-sized rounds. A nostalgic Lagos beach and park treat.

name: Eba & Egusi
description: Stiff cassava flour dough served with a rich melon-seed soup cooked with leafy greens and meat or fish. Lagos's most comforting complete meal.

name: Chin Chin
description: Crunchy, deep-fried dough strips seasoned with nutmeg and coconut. Sold in little bags everywhere — the Lagos snack you eat by the fistful.

name: Abacha Salad
description: Shredded dried cassava tossed in palm oil, ugba, garden eggs, crayfish, and ponmo. A vibrant, tangy Igbo salad beloved across Lagos.
